title: Host QQ16 correction temporaries in existing output banks
body:
[PR #3985](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3985)'s complete recovery word uses 112 extra full-cover temporary banks although 104 eventual output slots have no live output yet. This contribution derives those exact dependencies and gives a literal allocation inside the existing 224 owned output banks. All 224 original outputs still finish in F17, and all 224 borrowed current X/Y arrays remain unchanged.

Only Z_T (eight ports) is read before the future logger. Defer Z_U and Z_A; place the 104 query copies in those slots. Once all eight private queries have captured their inputs, eight query slots can become response slots. Restore Z_A while W_A is still unchanged, consume the responses, then define Z_U and resume the unchanged suffix. The checker records 104 exact query/response/output lifetime intervals and rejects early reuse, live-selected-output overwrite, initialization/frame/alias/return errors.

The complete local bill keeps **224 H1, 448 wrappers, 352 cover maps, 1,920 unit ADDs and 896 quarter ADDs**. Additional full-cover temporary banks fall **112→0**. Removing the 112 obsolete final temporary clears reduces CLEARs **536→424** and scalar allowance **27,184→26,960**. All first-use clears and original output definitions remain paid; arbitrary owned dirt is not assumed zero. Peak owner-private scratch stays 16.

This is concrete reuse under the pinned decoder's existing 224-owned-output contract, not a claim that these banks are free in the original gauge44 physical caller. The first-B1 cut is source-bound; six-tape placement, movement/control, output consumption, precision, family coverage and recursive supplier admission remain open. No kappa or optimality claim. The independently reviewed paired streaming construction uses a different access schedule and achieves 416 CLEARs / 26,944 scalar allowance with nine deferred outputs and zero future-private registers, versus this construction's 424 / 26,960, 104 deferred outputs and eight future-private registers. It is not a runtime dependency; this owner-private schedule is not claimed Pareto optimal.

Source: [PR #3985](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3985) head 400df7fca8f60c19bf163c77564fe3fbe9154b04, retaining only its exact WORD data and regenerating the full word from canonical [PR #2707](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2707). All transitive canonical inputs are SHA/Git-blob authenticated before executable reuse. Complete new-word replay checks both independent current arrays against the routed inverse and original arrays through F0/B1, all 73 frame coordinates, arbitrary 224 output dirt fields, borrowed return and 114,688 signed native columns with all 224 occurrences bound.

Validation: normal and optimized complete replay, six read-only/export/source/word/typed-receipt/overwrite boundary tests, metadata and input pins passed. Independent coordinating-agent code/proof review and frozen replay passed; exact hashes/scope are recorded. Hosted registered replay has passed; details follow. Final publication head and committed-byte/source-history checks follow below. Package: `research/qq16-output-pebbling`; reproduce with `python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/qq16-output-pebbling`.

Canonical main 20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90 remains unchanged, priority 6. User-assigned output-bank/register-allocation follow-up; shared claim https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3985#issuecomment-6263114494. Partial overlap coverage; no novelty guarantee.

Credit [PR #3985](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3985); ywz65 [PR #2707](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2707)/native methods; Arham Tahir [PR #2681](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2681) ordered inverse; Ali Romman's QQ16 lineage; commdata2338 [PR #2651](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2651) and Discussion 2617 for prior early-record/output-bank coalescing; Nick Petalas [PR #2722](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2722) access tariffs and [PR #3339](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3339) consumer ledger; retained geometry/native/supplier contributors. This concerns the newer zero-retention query/response lifetimes, not a second claim for [PR #2651](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2651)'s early-record saving. Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; independent AI review is distinguished from human/formal verification.

Publication head: `fb1c0da01c02f2a5fbc557dc16c1ebb90dac4e76`. Exact committed bytes (36 package/input files), canonical source-history ancestry, official Git-free export and export-integrity check, and diff whitespace check all passed. The full registered launcher has not been redundantly rerun locally; direct registered commands passed, and hosted registered replay has now passed.


Hosted validation completed successfully for publication head `fb1c0da01c02f2a5fbc557dc16c1ebb90dac4e76`: [Registered research packages run 39226247360](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39226247360). Completed replay-job logs bind merge `cc76758de4a12b5c9e66d64712ee499dc6f02d7e` to that exact head and canonical base `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`, using CPython 3.12.15. The complete mathematical replay passed, all six boundary tests passed in 215.245 seconds, and the full registered launcher reported `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/qq16-output-pebbling outcome=completed`. The committed-input check also passed with `git diff --exit-code`. This discharges the previously pending hosted registered-launcher check; mathematical and physical scope qualifications above remain unchanged.


The parallel hosted-streaming construction is now published separately as [PR #4015](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4015), head `0fff81d8997cef646538bcd4f60d7d455cf93b8e`. Its different access schedule attains the stronger local scalar/private counts already compared above; physical access tariffs remain to be compared.
